strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with clear practical relevance: addresses specific scalability issues in GANs (early layer inactivity and scale-coupled instability)
Strong empirical results: achieves competitive FID 2.96 on ImageNet-256 with only 40 epochs of training, demonstrating significant efficiency gains
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: systematic scaling studies across multiple model sizes (S/B/L/XL), thorough ablations validating each component, and robustness tests across patch sizes
Practical technical solutions: MNG, adaptive learning rate scaling, and latent space training are all straightforward to implement and integrate into existing frameworks
Excellent documentation and reproducibility materials: detailed implementation appendix, architectural specifications, hyperparameter tables, and extensive visual results
Clear presentation: generally well-written with informative figures and logical organization of contributions
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: MNG is an incremental extension of multi-scale supervision; learning rate scaling builds directly on equalized learning rates; transformer GANs and VAE-latent training are from prior work. Core contribution is primarily engineering-focused combination of existing techniques

Insufficient analysis of core method (MNG): lacks clear theoretical or empirical justification for specific noise schedules (0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0); no sensitivity analysis or principled design guidelines for practitioners applying to new domains

Narrow evaluation scope: single dataset (ImageNet-256) only; no unconditional generation results; missing standard metrics (Inception Score, precision/recall); no computational efficiency comparison (training time, memory, inference speed)

Reproducibility concerns: multiple manually-tuned design choices lack principled justification (latent guidance strength 1.1 applied to first 30% of blocks; manually-set loss weights λ_gp, λ_RGBM, λ_REBM; different hyperparameters per scale without clear scaling strategy); no released code mentioned

Limited ablation depth: adaptive LR improvements are modest with unclear statistical significance; REPA objective borrowed from prior work but inadequately motivated for GAN context; individual architectural contributions (RoPE, Layerscale, SwiGLU) not analyzed

Incomplete experimental analysis: unfair baseline comparisons (diffusion/flow models are fundamentally different); brief 40-epoch training makes it unclear if performance plateaus; non-standard FID evaluation (FID-50K/FID-5K distinction); patch size experiments show only marginal differences

Missing critical analyses: no frequency domain assessment of image quality; no evaluation of semantic diversity/coverage; no failure case discussion; limited investigation of which architectural choices actually drive performance gains

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with clear articulation of early layer inactivity and scale-coupled training instability in GANs
Technically sound methodology with mathematically formulated solutions (MNG strategy with Equations 2-3 and adaptive scaling rule in Equation 4)
Comprehensive ablation studies and experimental evaluation within the tested scope (model scaling, patch size robustness, GFLOPs correlation)
Strong empirical results on ImageNet-256 (FID 2.96 in 40 epochs) with consistent scaling behavior from S to XL model sizes
Good reproducibility documentation including detailed implementation details, model configurations, and training procedures in appendices
Extensive qualitative evaluations including latent space interpolations and intermediate feature visualizations demonstrating GAN properties preservation
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Primary contribution is combining existing techniques (ViT blocks, MSG-GAN-style multi-scale supervision, equalized learning rate principle) without fundamental new insights or methods

Insufficient evidence for MNG necessity: Ablation (Figure 5a) shows the method works reasonably without MNG; early layer 'inactivity' claims rely on visual evidence (Figure 4a) rather than quantitative metrics of activation degree

Severely limited experimental scope: All experiments restricted to single task (class-conditional ImageNet-256 generation); no unconditional generation, no high-resolution experiments, no evaluation on other domains or datasets

Weak baseline comparisons: Most comparisons against 2022 or earlier methods; insufficient quantitative comparison with recent diffusion/flow models; recent transformer-based generative models not adequately compared

Unsubstantiated efficiency claims: '6x fewer epochs' assertion lacks wall-clock time comparisons and detailed baseline training procedure documentation; different recipes make epoch-count comparisons unreliable

Lack of theoretical justification: Why VAE latent space is superior for transformers is asserted rather than explained; scaling rule (Eq. 4) is empirical without rigorous grounding; MNG's mechanism lacks rigorous analysis

Unexplored hyperparameter sensitivity: Multiple hyperparameters (λ_GP, λ_GP_AKI, λ_RBFM, noise schedules σ₁-σ₄) lack ablation; many techniques combined without clarifying which are essential versus optional
Limited evaluation metrics: Only FID-50K reported; no Inception Score, precision-recall, density-coverage, or human evaluation; FID can be gamed and doesn't always correlate with perceptual quality
Generalization claims unvalidated: Scaling rule only validated for one specific task; unclear if method generalizes to different architectures, resolutions, or class distributions

Missing critical analysis: No discussion of failure modes, limitations, or why the field shifted to diffusion models despite GAN advantages; no code availability mentioned despite reproducibility claims

strengths: Strong experimental results achieving state-of-the-art FID-50K of 2.96 on ImageNet-256 in just 40 epochs, demonstrating practical efficiency gains over baselines

Well-motivated technical contributions with Multi-level Noise-perturbed Guidance addressing early layer inactivity and adaptive learning rate scaling preventing training instability across model scales
Comprehensive ablation studies systematically validating both MNG (Section 3.3, Fig. 5) and adaptive learning rate (Fig. 5c) contributions, plus per-block influence analysis (Fig. 4)
Rigorous experimental evaluation including scalability across model sizes, patch size robustness, discriminator-generator coupled scaling analysis, and feature visualization
Excellent reproducibility with detailed implementation specifications (Section A.1), complete model configurations (Table 2), and hyperparameter transparency
Successful demonstration of transformer scalability for GANs from Small to XL models with maintained training stability
Clear presentation with well-structured methodology and effective visualizations of architecture, results, and qualitative examples
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty—Multi-level Noise Guidance adapts MSG-GAN without substantial modification, and adaptive LR scaling conceptually relates to existing equalized learning rate approaches (Karras et al., 2017); primary novelty is engineering combination
Single-dataset evaluation—Only ImageNet-256 quantitatively reported; missing evaluation on CelebA-HQ, FFHQ, and other resolutions limits assessment of generalization across domains

Incomplete computational cost analysis—Only reports epoch counts without wall-clock time or FLOP comparisons; transformers' per-iteration computational overhead relative to CNNs remains unquantified despite fewer epochs

Insufficient theoretical justification—Adaptive LR scaling rule (Eq. 4) is empirically motivated but lacks rigorous theoretical grounding explaining why this particular scaling relationship is optimal

Comparison fairness concerns—Table 1 mixes baselines from different years with varying training protocols and VAE setups, making definitive performance ranking difficult without equal-budget comparison

Missing analysis of transformer architectural advantages—No investigation of attention patterns, architectural ablations, or conceptual explanation of why transformers outperform CNNs for GANs beyond latent-space encoding
Limited failure analysis—No exploration of failure modes, challenging image categories, VAE quality impact, or discussion of when MNG provides benefits versus drawbacks
VAE dependency insufficiently explored—No ablation on pre-trained VAE quality or investigation of whether VAE limitations constrain generation quality and end-to-end training feasibility

strengths: Systematic and important research direction: First thorough study of GAN scalability, filling a genuine gap compared to diffusion/AR literature
Strong empirical results: State-of-the-art FID 2.18 on ImageNet-256 in 60 epochs (4× fewer than strong baselines), demonstrating significant data efficiency gains

Well-motivated problem identification: Early-layer inactivity convincingly demonstrated via feature visualization, block ablations, and quantitative metrics; scale-coupled instability clearly identified

Comprehensive experimental validation: Thorough ablations (Fig. 5), scaling studies across 4 model sizes, multiple datasets (ImageNet-256/512, COCO, FFHQ), multiple metrics (FID, CLIP-FID, Precision/Recall)
Excellent presentation and reproducibility: Detailed implementation details, model configurations with parameter counts, extensive appendix with visualizations and supplementary experiments
Strong scalability analysis: Clear power-law scaling relationship (FID ∝ C^-0.456) and consistent performance improvements across model sizes demonstrate reliable scaling behavior
Practical utility: Latent space supports semantic manipulation (interpolation, editing with GANSpace/StyleCLIP); 200× speedup in inference over 250-step diffusion models
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Individual components are well-known (transformers, VAE latent training, intermediate supervision similar to MSGGAN, LR scaling); main novelty is systematic scalability study rather than fundamental methodological contributions

MNG design lacks principled justification: Exponential noise schedule chosen empirically over linear but no rigorous justification; specific α values (0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0) appear arbitrary; sensitivity analysis absent; connection to MSGGAN insufficiently explored

Width-aware LR rule justification incomplete: Appendix A.10 provides simplified linear layer analysis but not rigorous proof; assumes normalized unit-variance activations; depth scaling deferred to future work; the ηₐdₐₚₜ ∝ 1/C rule is relatively straightforward

Inadequate analysis of key finding: Figure 6a shows discriminator scaling matters more than generator scaling but this interesting result is largely unexplored; missing analysis of what discriminator learns and why D-scaling is more effective
Statistical significance concerns: Only 3 random seeds for GAT-S/2 at 10 epochs; multi-seed validation across all model sizes would strengthen scalability claims

Fairness of experimental comparisons: StyleGAN-XL uses ImageNet-pretrained discriminators (potentially biasing FID); different training recipes not fully standardized; limited 1-NFE baselines (mostly multi-step methods)

Practical efficiency claims need clarification: GAT is ~5× slower per iteration than DiT; wall-clock time comparison uses different hardware (8×A100 vs RTX A6000) and doesn't fully account for discriminator overhead; claimed advantages should be more carefully contextualized

Limited exploration of design space: Why K=4 intermediate outputs specifically? No ablation on number of supervision levels; generalization only tested on ImageNet-512 and COCO; no evaluation on highly diverse datasets

Incomplete analysis of failure modes: No discussion of when approach struggles; FFHQ unconditional results less impressive than ImageNet, reasons unexplored; depth-dependent scaling not systematically studied

strengths: Comprehensive experimental validation with systematic scaling studies across model sizes; power-law relationship well-established (Fig 3d)
Thorough ablation studies clearly isolating contributions of MNG, adaptive LR, and REPA with quantitative metrics (Section 3.4)
Strong empirical results: SOTA single-step generation on ImageNet-256 (FID 2.18) with improved data efficiency (60 vs 240-480 epochs for baselines)
Well-characterized diagnostic analysis: early layer inactivity quantified through feature visualization, block ablation studies, and cosine similarity metrics (Figs 4, 13)
Practical value from single-step inference (~200× speedup) and compatibility with large-batch training (Fig 8)
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Individual components are established (TransGAN/ViTGAN, MSG-GAN, LDM, width scaling heuristics, REPA from diffusion). Claims scalability through combination rather than fundamental insight

Insufficient isolation of scaling drivers: No ablation comparing pixel-space vs VAE space GAN; REPA ablation shows catastrophic 15.3→69 FID drop (Fig 5c), making core contribution unclear. Which component actually enables scaling?

Weak MNG justification: Exponential schedule choice over linear (MNG-lin) is empirical; MSG-GAN performs worse but 'why noise is fundamentally better' explanation is speculative. Noise schedule hyperparameters (0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0) appear arbitrary without sensitivity analysis

Mathematical rigor concerns: Width-aware LR derivation (A.10) assumes N(0,1) i.i.d. hidden vectors, violated under normalization. No empirical validation that per-step output changes actually remain constant across widths. Power-law exponent (-0.456) differs from diffusion (~-0.5), unexplained

Experimental fairness issues: GAT vs baselines use different epochs (60 vs 240-480) on different hardware (RTX A6000 vs A100); unclear if equal-compute comparisons. StyleGAN-XL uses ImageNet-pretrained discriminators while GAT uses DINOv2—apples-to-oranges

Limited scope: Primarily ImageNet-256; ImageNet-512 shows marginal gains (4.02→4.04); MS-COCO extension (MM-GAT, FID 7.98) lags U-ViT (5.4) and authors call it 'deliberately lightweight'; unconditional generation only on FFHQ-256
Reproducibility concerns: No code release mentioned; extremely high compute cost (8×A6000 GPUs); seed sensitivity only tested for GAT-S/2 at 10 epochs; 'Project page:.' blank in paper

Missing mechanistic analysis: No analysis of gradient flow validating width-aware LR intuition; training stability/divergence rates not reported; why MSG-GAN fails needs ablation beyond speculation about 'cross-scale consistency'

Absent baselines: No pixel-space transformer GAN comparison; no evaluation of other recent transformer architectures or other domains (medical imaging, textures) where GANs excel; limited discussion of when single-step GANs remain preferable to diffusion models

strengths: Addresses important understudied problem: GAN scalability has been underexplored compared to diffusion/autoregressive models, despite GANs' advantages (single-step inference, semantic latent space)
Thorough problem analysis with multiple diagnostic approaches: Early-layer inactivity demonstrated via feature visualization, block ablation (LPIPS), and cosine similarity metrics across noise inputs

Well-motivated solutions: MNG elegantly simplifies MSG-GAN's multi-scale supervision via noise perturbation; width-aware LR scaling is principled with clear intuition about output magnitude scaling with channel dimension

Comprehensive experimental validation: Extensive ablations (Fig. 5) showing individual contributions, scaling analysis across 4 model sizes, power-law fitting, multiple evaluation metrics (FID, CLIP-FID, precision/recall), and extensions to multiple domains

Strong empirical results: FID 2.18 on ImageNet-256 in 60 epochs is competitive with StyleGAN-XL (2.30), GigaGAN (3.45), MeanFlow (3.43) while requiring 4-8× fewer epochs; ~200× faster inference than 250-step diffusion models
Excellent presentation and reproducibility: Clear problem motivation, well-designed figures, detailed implementation details in appendix, reasonable effort toward reproducibility
Useful broader analyses: Decoupled G/D scaling analysis, representation alignment via CKNNA, compatibility with large-batch training and different tokenizers
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Multi-scale supervision (MSG-GAN, diffusion) and learning rate adjustment are well-known ideas; contribution is refining them for GANs rather than fundamental innovation. Heavily combines existing components (VAE tokenization, ViT, REPA from diffusion work)

Weak theoretical justification for width-aware LR rule: A.10 relies on strong assumptions (independent unit-variance channels, linear approximation) that may not hold in deep residual transformers with normalization. No empirical validation of η·C ≈ constant principle across depths/batch sizes

MNG design choices appear ad-hoc: Exponential noise schedule (0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0) justified only by empirical comparison to linear schedule; K=4 intermediate outputs unexplained; cumulative noise construction (ε_{k-1} = r_k ε_k + σ_k η_k) not deeply motivated

Heavy dependence on pre-trained components limits novelty: Frozen VAE reduces independence; REPA (Vision Foundation Model alignment) is directly borrowed from recent diffusion work (Yu et al., 2025) with Fig. 5c showing massive FID degradation without it (~69 vs. 15.3); unclear what is GAN-specific vs. diffusion technique transfer

Incomplete comparison fairness: StyleGAN-XL marked with † for using ImageNet-pretrained discriminators; MeanFlow uses guided flow fields (different setup); some GigaGAN comparisons lack epoch information; missing comparisons with other recent transformer-based GAN scaling work

Significant computational barriers to reproducibility: Training 5× longer per iteration than DiT; GAT-XL/2 requires ~18 days on 8×RTX A6000 GPUs; this severely limits practical reproducibility and adoption

Limited multi-seed evaluation: Only 3 random seeds for GAT-S/2 at 10 epochs (A.16) showing FID-5K range of ~2.2 points; no multi-seed results for main model (GAT-XL/2) or other scales, limiting confidence in claimed improvements

Incomplete ablation of component interactions: While individual ablations provided, combined ablations missing (Does MNG work without REPA? How much does width-aware LR help without MNG?), making it unclear if components are complementary or redundant

Modest improvements in some settings: FID 2.30→2.18 vs. StyleGAN-XL (3.9%) with different training setup; only 1.25 FID point better than MeanFlow despite 4× more epochs (60 vs. 240); state-of-the-art claim narrowly scoped to 1-NFE setting

Missing justifications for design choices: Why RoPE, SwiGLU-FFN, qk-normalization over alternatives? Why Layerscale initialized to 0.1? Limited sensitivity analysis for critical hyperparameters beyond patch size (p=2 default)
